content.intro: Value Types and Reference Types is lesson 21 in Variables, Data Types, and Constants. Types define which values an expression can represent and which operations are valid. Make conversions and null handling visible rather than relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: The type system catches many mistakes early, but only when you choose types and conversions deliberately. This lesson focuses on value types and reference types and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

items.title: Understanding value types
items.text: A value-type assignment copies the value; copying a reference-type variable copies the reference, so both variables may refer to the same object. Test with a small before/after example to see which state is shared.

items.title: Understanding reference types
items.text: A value-type assignment copies the value; copying a reference-type variable copies the reference, so both variables may refer to the same object. Test with a small before/after example to see which state is shared.

items.title: Assignment and copying behavior
items.text: A value-type assignment copies the value; copying a reference-type variable copies the reference, so both variables may refer to the same object. Test with a small before/after example to see which state is shared.
